title: Investigation of Wiener filter techniques for in-loop filtering in video coding
description: A doctoral thesis on Wiener-filter techniques for in-loop filtering in video coding.
abstract: This thesis investigates how Wiener-filter-based in-loop filtering can improve video coding efficiency and reduce visible compression artifacts. It studies classification strategies based on multiple image features, sparse shearlet-domain representations, and convolutional neural networks. The resulting methods combine analytical signal processing with data-driven classification to preserve image structure, improve subjective quality, and strengthen coding performance.

title: Shearlet-based intensity classification loop filter for video coding
description: A journal article on shearlet-based intensity classification for loop filtering in video coding.
abstract: This paper introduces a non-data-driven in-loop filter for Versatile Video Coding that uses a sparse shearlet transform to distinguish important image structures from quantization noise. Shearlet coefficients are grouped by intensity and reconstructed with class-specific Wiener filtering, reducing compression artifacts while preserving edges and textures. Tests on JVET sequences report average bit-rate reductions of up to 1.5% beyond VVC together with improved subjective image quality.
venue: Signal Processing: Image Communication, volume 115, article 116967
authors: Johannes Erfurt; Wang-Q Lim; Jonathan Pfaff; Heiko Schwarz; Detlev Marpe; Thomas Wiegand

title: Adaptive Loop Filter with a CNN-Based Classification
description: A conference paper on CNN-based classification for adaptive loop filtering.
abstract: This work generalizes the classification and finite-impulse-response filtering stages of the VVC adaptive loop filter into a convolutional-neural-network architecture. The learned classifier and filtering process form a data-driven in-loop filter that remains closely connected to the conventional ALF design. Experiments report average bit-rate savings between 3.85% and 4.75% for all-intra coding and between 4.33% and 4.39% for random-access coding, depending on the quantization-parameter range.
venue: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), pages 1836-1840
authors: Wang-Q Lim; Jonathan Pfaff; Björn Stallenberger; Johannes Erfurt; Heiko Schwarz; Detlev Marpe; Thomas Wiegand

title: Extended multiple feature-based classifications for adaptive loop filtering
description: A journal article on multiple feature-based classifications for adaptive loop filtering.
abstract: This paper examines how adaptive loop filtering can benefit from several complementary image-feature classifications instead of relying on one classifier. It extends multiple feature-based ALF by integrating sample adaptive offset filtering and introduces block-based classifications intended to lower complexity. The experiments show that the extended method improves compression efficiency over the original multiple-classification approach.
venue: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing, volume 8, article e28
authors: Johannes Erfurt; Wang-Q Lim; Heiko Schwarz; Detlev Marpe; Thomas Wiegand

title: A Study of the Perceptually Weighted Peak Signal-To-Noise Ratio (WPSNR) for Image Compression
description: A conference paper studying perceptually weighted peak signal-to-noise ratio for image compression.
abstract: This study revisits perceptually weighted PSNR as an efficient alternative to conventional image-quality metrics for compressed images. It evaluates a block-based method that weights regions according to visual sensitivity and introduces a sample-based variant with more spatially precise weighting. On JPEG and JPEG 2000 content, the proposed measures approximate subjective quality ratings more accurately than PSNR, SSIM, and related perceptual metrics while remaining computationally inexpensive.
venue: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), pages 2339-2343
authors: Johannes Erfurt; Christian R. Helmrich; Sebastian Bosse; Heiko Schwarz; Detlev Marpe; Thomas Wiegand
